source_title: ‘Young and the Restless’ Star Roger Howarth Says He’s ‘So Happy’ to Be a Soap Actor as He Wins at 2026 Daytime Emmys - People.com
source_excerpt:
Howarth’s win at this year’s award ceremony marks his first in 32 years
Roger Howarth won Outstanding Supporting Actor in a Daytime Drama Series at the 2026 Daytime Emmys
Howarth stars as Matt Clark in The Young and the Restless
The actor’s win marks his first victory in 32 years
Roger Howarth won his first Daytime Emmy award in 32 years!
The actor, 58, won Outstanding Supporting Actor in a Drama Series for his portrayal of Matt Clark in The Young and the Restless at the 53rd Daytime Emmys on Friday, Oct. 30. Howarth’s victory comes over three decades after he won in 1994 for One Life to Live .
“I’m really, really happy. I love being an actor. I’m so happy that I get to do this thing that we all get to do together, that we cooperate,” Howarth said in his acceptance speech. “I share this with Josh Griffith, Joe Shelby Griffith, and I want to say thank you to CBS and to Sony.”
Howarth thanked The Young and the Restless cast and crew “that have made me feel so welcome that I don’t know how to say thank you other than to just say thank you. I appreciate you.”
Howarth joined The Young and the Restless in 2025. His first major soap opera role was as Todd Manning on One Life to Live. Howarth’s portrayal of the show’s villain earned him a Daytime Emmy in 1994 in the now-defunct Outstanding Younger Leading Actor in a Drama Series category.
His nomination at this year’s ceremony marks his first Emmy nod in 21 years. In an interview with Soap Opera Digest , Howarth opened up about what the recognition means to him. “I’m just happy to be still in consideration and above ground,” he said. “Both of those things are pretty great. I mean, I was barely old enough to drive when I won the first one!”
Other nominees included Lawrence Saint-Victor for The Bold and the Beautiful , Timon Kyle Durrett and Mike Manning for Beyond the Gates and Sean Dominic and Michael Graziadei for The Young and the Restless .
Saint-Victor, 44, stars on The Bold and the Beautiful as Carter Walton, the handsome lawyer and COO of Forrester Creations. The actor is also nominated for Outstanding Writing Team, as he joined the show’s team in 2015. Saint-Victor makes history as the first Black actor to be nominated in both categories in the same year.
Speaking to Ebony on what his nominations mean to him, Saint-Victor said, “So many Black men and women, both in front of and behind the camera, pushed the door open and kept pushing so that I could walk through. … I don’t take for granted that I get to stand on the other side of those doors now.”
“Do I think about what it would be like if I won? Of course I do. But the truth is, I feel like I already have,” he continued. “I get to create opportunities for representation. I get to help show the world that Black people are wonderfully and beautifully complex. That means everything to me.”
Durrett, 53, stars as Bill Hamilton, the ruthless criminal defense attorney, in Beyond the Gates . His nomination at this year’s ceremony marks his first-ever Daytime Emmy nod. In an interview with WHNT-TV, a local news station in Huntsville, Ala., Durrett explained what his consideration means to not only him, but the Black community.
“It feels good because I’m tapping into something that is historic among our people,” Durrett said. Beyond the Gates is the first-ever daytime soap opera with a primarily Black cast, as it follows the Dupree family, a wealthy Black dynasty, as they navigate love, legacy and secrecy.
In Beyond the Gates , Manning, 39, stars as Bradley “Smitty” Smith, the charming husband to Congressman Martin Richardson (Brandon Clayton). Manning originally auditioned for the role of Derek, played by daytime newcomer Ben Gavin. But when production pitched him as Smitty, Manning told TV Source Magazine that he was drawn to the idea of getting to play a character who was both a loving father and investigative journalist.
Manning’s nomination marks his sixth Emmy nod and is one of 15 nods for Beyond the Gates. Celebrating this accomplishment, Manning shared photos of him and his castmates on set on Instagram , writing, “Yesterday was a whirlwind… I’m so proud of every single person who makes @beyondthegatescbs possible & consider myself blessed to be part of Fairmont Crest. Thank you to everyone who has shown love for our show. I’m still floating.”
Dominic, 48, stars as Dr. Nate Hastings, a passionate doctor who works at Genoa City Memorial Hospital, in The Young and the Restless. Dominic made his daytime television debut in 2019 on the CBS soap opera.
Speaking to Soap Central about his first-ever Emmy nod, Dominic thanked former Young and the Restless executive producer Josh Griffith. “[He] gave me a prime story. I’m grateful that I was able to bring it to life and be recognized by my peers,” he said.
In The Young and the Restless, Graziadei, 47, stars as Daniel Romalotti Jr. and has portrayed him on and off for 14 years. His nod at the 2026 Daytime Emmys marks the fourth in his career. Speaking to Soap Opera Digest , Graziadei said the best part of the annual ceremony is seeing his castmates.
“[Everyone’s] all dressed up and cheering for each other,” he said. “And when people do win from the show, it’s always nice to be there and be supportive of them.”
